title: Reactions of Acids and Useful Salts
summary: Acids react with metals to make hydrogen and with carbonates to make carbon dioxide. Plus the salts in your kitchen and medicine cabinet.

ib.note: General equations and gas tests extended in MYP 4

cbse.chapter: Ch 2: Acids, Bases and Salts (reactions with metals and carbonates; common salts)

objectives: I can write general word equations for acids with metals and with carbonates.
I can describe the tests for hydrogen (squeaky pop) and carbon dioxide (lime water).
I can name the salt produced from a given acid and metal or carbonate.
I can describe everyday uses of common salts (baking soda, washing soda, plaster of Paris, bleaching powder).
misconceptions: All metals react with acids (copper, silver and gold don't react with dilute acids).
The gas from any fizzing reaction is oxygen.
Baking soda and baking powder are the same thing.
